verdict_text:
YES

The plan loads base and adapter under separate aliases, computes `B @ A` in float32 per layer via a regex matmul, scales by 2, upcasts the base weight to float32, adds the delta, and casts back to float16, matching the required-result clause. Intermediate `delta` tensors and the whole `lora::` namespace are deleted before output, so no adapter or intermediate tensor can be written. All four required checks appear as `assert` transforms before the output step (16 `lora_A` found, 16 deltas merged, no `lora_` name remaining, layer-0 shape `[6144, 2048]`, exactly 244 tensors). Output is safetensors under `out/T5` with a 512 MiB shard cap, which satisfies the at-most constraint and stores the two 206 MB embeddings alone as required.
